statements.text: The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that the government assesses the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard. He said the UK will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks and bring further sanctions to restrict Iran and the IRGC.

The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that new funding has been announced to help Ukraine get through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and that a new sanctions package means over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity is now covered by UK sanctions.

The Prime Minister said an energy ceasefire, with both sides stopping their attacks, is the quickest way to get diesel back onto world markets without rewarding the aggressor. He said he raised this with President Trump in New York and welcomed Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire. He said President Zelenskyy assured him Ukraine would immediately implement it once a start date is confirmed.

The Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks, and is set to tell President Zelenskyy so when they meet. The UK says it will double down on support for Ukraine.

At their meeting at Downing Street on 14 October, the leaders reflected on their call and on Russia's attacks on civilians and energy infrastructure since President Trump called for an energy ceasefire. The leaders underlined that Russia had no interest in peace.

The UK will accelerate deliveries of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which the government says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. The UK has already committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of them to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of a £45 million package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter needs. At the 14 October meeting, the Prime Minister set out the UK's latest package of these missiles.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: The UK is standing by plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian liquefied natural gas exports. Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said he would urge partners at the IMF meetings in Bangkok to implement an equivalent ban, and said: I urge partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, like we have done in the UK, to curtail the war chest funding Putin so desperately wants.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK's rock-solid support for Ukraine is vital for keeping the UK safe, that the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes and will go further and faster, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent.

The Prime Minister told the Commons that Britain has decided to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling. He said a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions, and he condemned the attacks on King Khalid International Airport.

The Prime Minister said Russia is conducting a campaign of hybrid attacks and sabotage across Europe. He said that in Berlin he and Chancellor Merz agreed a new partnership to tackle these hybrid threats.

The Prime Minister confirmed the UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table, he said, are a trade deal on food and drink, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration. He said a food and drink trade deal would add the equivalent of over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040.

The Prime Minister said the agreement on the table would lift a burden that can reach £1,400 on a single shipment for farmers and food producers. For small businesses, he said it would mean no more export health certificates, which can cost up to £200 each time.

The Prime Minister made a serious and genuine offer to the Scottish Government to work together on pushing power out of Westminster and Holyrood. He proposed designing together a new model of regional economic empowerment across Scotland, through the No10 North and Scotland Office channels, with innovation, enterprise and employability funding devolved at UK level and an offer of DWP devolution for localised employment support. He said the National Economic Council would meet the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in a couple of weeks.

Douglas Alexander said the Prime Minister's offer to the Scottish Government is a genuine one, and that the Scotland Office is ready to roll up its sleeves alongside the Scottish Government to make it happen.
The Prime Minister said Scotland, the most devolved nation in the UK, is one of the most centralised nations in Europe.

The Prime Minister said that when the UK takes up the G20 presidency in 2027 it will place AI centre stage, capturing its opportunities while guarding against its risks, and will work towards a single set of global principles and standards on AI.

The Prime Minister said he raised the Falkland Islands and the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British with President Trump, and that the UK will always do whatever it takes to uphold the islanders' will.

A UK government spokesperson said Ukraine has repeatedly demonstrated it is serious about peace, but Russia has repeatedly rejected full and partial ceasefires while continuing attacks on Ukrainian civilians and energy, and said Russia could end the war today.

Great British Railways' new headquarters site at Becketwell, Derby, was unveiled on 15 October. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029. The HQ is estimated to bring an £151 million boost to Derby's economy and hundreds of rail jobs, and will accommodate up to 450 GBR staff.

Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship, with the first starters based in Derby. The government says this matters at a time when less than 7% of the railway's workforce is under 25.
Andy Burnham said that for too long people have put up with a railway that often lets them down, and that today is another big step forward.

Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, and that Great British Railways will bring the railway together around one mission, better services for passengers, with Derby at the heart of its future.

Pat McFadden said the Derby foundation apprenticeship forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package, which he said is creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn.
Claire Ward said the news is fantastic for Derby, and that she is particularly pleased about the 600 apprenticeship places.

The Prime Minister said the government assesses that the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard. He said the government will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks and will bring further sanctions to restrict Iran and the IRGC's capacity to do harm.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire. He said President Zelenskyy has assured him Ukraine would immediately implement it once a start date is confirmed, and that he will discuss this further with President Zelenskyy in the coming days.

The Prime Minister told the Commons on 12 October that the government has announced new funding to help Ukraine through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package that covers over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity.

On 13 October the UK said the Prime Minister would host President Zelenskyy at Downing Street, and on 14 October the two leaders met there. The leaders discussed how the UK could accelerate defensive support to Ukraine ahead of the winter, and underlined that Russia had no interest in peace.

The UK will accelerate deliveries of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which the government says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. The UK has already committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of them to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of a £45 million missile package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter needs.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that supporting Ukraine is not just the right thing to do but the necessary thing, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor John Healey is urging partners at the IMF meetings in Bangkok to fully implement an equivalent ban on Russian LNG to the UK's, and said he urged partners to back the ban to curtail the war chest funding Putin.

The Prime Minister confirmed the UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. He said the agenda includes a trade deal on food and drink, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a youth experience scheme, and deeper cooperation on immigration.

The Prime Minister said a food and drink trade deal is projected to add the equivalent of over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040, and that it would lift a burden that can reach £1,400 on a single shipment for farmers and food producers.
The Prime Minister said the proposed energy deal could cut wholesale energy costs in Northern Ireland by 20%.

Andy Burnham said he is making an offer to the Scottish Government to work together on pushing more power out of Westminster and Holyrood. He said the offer is part of a speech in which he will invite the First Minister to work with him on regional empowerment.

Douglas Alexander said power was never supposed to stop at the doors of the Scottish Parliament, and that the Prime Minister's offer to the Scottish Government is a genuine one, with the Scotland Office ready to work alongside it.

In his 16 October speech in Motherwell, the Prime Minister offered Scotland a model of localised employment support similar to England's, shaped by Holyrood. He said the National Economic Council would meet in a couple of weeks with the First Ministers of Scotland and Wales and the First and Deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland, the first such meeting since he became Prime Minister.

The Prime Minister said the Scottish Government has agreed this week to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west of Scotland.

Construction of the Great British Railways headquarters at Becketwell in Derby is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029. The government says the HQ will bring hundreds of rail jobs and an estimated £151 million boost to Derby's economy, and it will accommodate up to 450 GBR staff.

Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship, with the first starters based in Derby. Pat McFadden said this forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn.

The Prime Minister confirmed Britain's decision to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling support, and said a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions.

The Prime Minister said he and Chancellor Merz agreed in Berlin a new partnership to tackle Russian hybrid threats, and that he confirmed a commitment to establish a new National Centre for Information Defence.

The Prime Minister confirmed that AI will be centre stage in the UK's G20 presidency in 2027, and said the UK aims to work towards agreeing a single set of global principles and standards on AI during that year.

The Prime Minister said he raised the Falkland Islands and the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British with President Trump, and said the government will always do whatever it takes to uphold the islanders' will.
